issue: IDOR: getOrderById returns any order to any authenticated user with no ownership or admin check
evidence: const order = await Order.findById(req.params.id).populate('user', 'name email')  // no check order.user === req.user._id
recommendation: After loading the order, reject with 403 unless order.user.equals(req.user._id) || req.user.isAdmin. The route /api/orders/:id is only behind 'protect', so any logged-in user can enumerate ObjectIds and read other customers' orders, including shipping address and PayPal payer email.

issue: updateOrderToPaid marks an order paid with no ownership check and no server-side payment verification
evidence: order.isPaid = true; order.paymentResult = { id: req.body.id, status: req.body.status, ... email_address: req.body.payer.email_address }
recommendation: Verify the order belongs to req.user (or is admin), and verify the payment server-side against the PayPal API (capture lookup) instead of trusting client-supplied req.body. As written, any authenticated user can PUT /api/orders/:id/pay on any order and mark it paid with fabricated payment data, bypassing payment entirely.

issue: JWT verified with no algorithm allow-list on a vulnerable jsonwebtoken 8.5.1
evidence: const decoded = jwt.verify(token, process.env.JWT_SECRET)  // no { algorithms: ['HS256'] }
recommendation: Pin algorithms: jwt.verify(token, secret, { algorithms: ['HS256'] }) and upgrade jsonwebtoken to >=9. jsonwebtoken <=8.5.1 has GHSA-qwph-4952-7xr6 (insecure default algorithm in verify) and GHSA-hjrf-2m68-5959 (RSA->HMAC key confusion); without an explicit algorithm list these enable signature-bypass / token forgery.

issue: Feature-flags API has no authentication; full flag config exposed publicly
evidence: app.use('/api/feature-flags', featureFlagRoutes)  // routes have no protect/admin
recommendation: The only access control on the feature-flags admin is a client-side useEffect redirect in FeatureFlagsScreen.jsx (trivially bypassed). GET /api/feature-flags and /:featureId leak internal rollout strategy, targeted_segments and dependency topology to anonymous users. Add protect+admin to read routes (or scope what is returned) and never rely on the React guard for authorization.

issue: Unsanitised user input used directly as a MongoDB $regex (ReDoS / regex injection)
recommendation: req.query.keyword is passed verbatim into a regex. A crafted keyword (e.g. nested quantifiers) causes catastrophic backtracking and CPU exhaustion (ReDoS) on a public endpoint. Escape regex metacharacters or use a MongoDB text index / $text search, and cap keyword length.

issue: Hardcoded fallback JWT secret 'replace_with_dev_secret' baked into compose default
recommendation: The same weak default secret also appears in .env.example and AGENTS.md. If anyone ships without overriding JWT_SECRET, all tokens are forgeable with a publicly known key. Remove the inline fallback so the stack fails fast when JWT_SECRET is unset, and require a strong random secret. generateToken.js / authMiddleware.js perform no length or strength check on the secret.

issue: No rate limiting or lockout on login or registration endpoints
recommendation: POST /api/users/login and POST /api/users allow unlimited attempts, enabling credential stuffing / brute force and registration abuse. Add a rate limiter (e.g. express-rate-limit, 5-10 attempts / 15 min per IP) on the auth routes.

issue: No server-side input validation on registration / profile update (no schema, no password policy)
evidence: const { name, email, password } = req.body; await User.create({ name, email, password })
recommendation: Email format is never validated, and there is no minimum password strength — '123456' is accepted (see data/users.js seeds). Add server-side validation (e.g. express-validator / Joi) for email format, name length, and a password policy. Relying on Mongoose 'required' only is insufficient.

issue: Mass-assignment risk: profile update trusts req.body fields directly
evidence: user.email = req.body.email || user.email  // admin updateUser sets user.isAdmin = req.body.isAdmin
recommendation: updateUserProfile lets a user freely change their email with no uniqueness re-check or verification (account takeover via duplicate/typo'd email). In the admin updateUser, user.isAdmin = req.body.isAdmin is assigned unconditionally; if isAdmin is omitted it becomes undefined and silently demotes. Whitelist and validate each updatable field explicitly.

issue: Password pre-save hook missing return after next(), re-hashes already-hashed passwords
evidence: if (!this.isModified('password')) { next() }  // no return; falls through to bcrypt.hash
recommendation: When password is NOT modified the hook calls next() but does not return, so it continues and re-hashes the stored (already bcrypt) hash, corrupting credentials on any profile save that touches the user document. Add 'return next()'. This is both a correctness and an auth-availability (account lockout) issue.

issue: Multiple known-vulnerable backend dependencies (16 advisories: 1 critical, 10 high)
evidence: jsonwebtoken ^8.5.1, multer ^1.4.2 (busboy/dicer GHSA-wm7h-9275-46v2), body-parser/qs DoS, mongoose/bson chain
recommendation: npm audit reports 16 vulnerabilities. Notably jsonwebtoken<=8.5.1 (signature bypass), multer<=2.1.0 via dicer (HeaderParser crash DoS on the public /api/upload), and body-parser/qs DoS. Upgrade jsonwebtoken to >=9 and multer to >=2.x, then re-run audit; isolate the upgrade per repo convention.

issue: react-scripts pinned to 3.4.3 (2020) — large transitive vulnerability surface
recommendation: react-scripts 3.4.3 drags in years-old webpack/babel/postcss/node-forge transitive deps with many published advisories and is incompatible with modern OpenSSL (the repo works around it with --openssl-legacy-provider). Plan an upgrade of the CRA toolchain (or migrate the build) as an isolated change; track the dev-server / build-chain CVEs explicitly.

issue: File upload validates only by extension/MIME string and enforces no size limit
evidence: const filetypes = /jpg|jpeg|png/; multer({ storage }) // no limits: { fileSize }
owasp: A08 Software and Data Integrity Failures
recommendation: checkFileType trusts a client-supplied filename and the easily-spoofed file.mimetype, and multer has no limits.fileSize, allowing disk-exhaustion DoS and upload of disguised content. Add limits: { fileSize }, validate real content (magic bytes), randomise stored filenames, and confirm POST /api/upload requires admin (it currently has no protect/admin middleware at all — anyone can write files into uploads/).

issue: No security HTTP headers, no CORS policy, and no JSON body-size limit
evidence: app.use(express.json())  // no helmet, no cors config, no { limit }
recommendation: The app sets no security headers (helmet: HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, frame-ancestors/CSP), and express.json() has the default 100kb but no explicit cap or rate limiting, leaving the API open to clickjacking, MIME sniffing and large-payload abuse. Add helmet and an explicit express.json({ limit }) and consider a global rate limiter.

issue: JWT (30-day, non-revocable) stored in localStorage — exposed to any XSS
evidence: localStorage.setItem('userInfo', JSON.stringify(data))  // data.token is the bearer JWT
recommendation: Per generateToken.js the JWT lives 30 days and (ADR-0003) cannot be revoked server-side. Storing it in localStorage means any XSS (or malicious dependency in the large CRA tree) can exfiltrate a long-lived admin token. Prefer httpOnly+Secure+SameSite cookies, shorten token lifetime, and add a refresh/rotation mechanism.

issue: Raw error objects logged to console; no security audit logging for auth events
owasp: A09 Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
recommendation: Auth failures, admin actions (user delete, role change, feature-flag writes) and payment changes are not audit-logged, while jwt verification errors dump full stack traces to stdout. Add structured audit logging for security-relevant events and avoid logging full token/verification internals.

issue: Embedding/Qdrant hosts come from env with no allow-list; query text forwarded to internal services
evidence: await fetch(`${OLLAMA_URL}/api/embeddings`, ...); new QdrantClient({ url: QDRANT_URL })
recommendation: OLLAMA_URL / QDRANT_URL are taken from environment with no validation; if an attacker can influence these env vars (or a future variant accepts a per-request URL), the MCP server can be pointed at arbitrary internal endpoints. Pin to a fixed allow-list of hosts and validate the scheme/host before issuing requests.

issue: PAYPAL_CLIENT_ID returned via unauthenticated endpoint that echoes raw env value
recommendation: The PayPal client id is public by design, but the endpoint blindly res.send()s whatever is in the env var with no presence check; a misconfigured deployment could leak an unintended secret placed there, and an empty value yields a confusing 200/empty body. Validate the value and return a typed JSON response.
